title: Runtime compile audit and synthetic benchmark catalog for MHA/GQA/MoE
creator: Marisol Ortega
description: Goal: Create an auditable compilation and kernel-selection catalog driven by deterministic synthetic benchmarks that exercise MHA, GQA, and MoE execution paths. Deliverables: 1) a documented catalog of compile profiles per architecture variant (fp16/amp/quantized) with provenance and verification hashes; 2) a small synthetic-benchmark suite that reproduces representative token-length distributions and expert-shard patterns; 3) a pin-validation job that verifies a candidate profile meets latency & correctness gates before publishing to the profile registry. Motivation: teams onboarding new hybrid attention / MoE-style models have observed non-deterministic kernel selection across infra generations. This leads to regressions when pins are published or when rollback is needed. A reproducible audit + benchmark catalog will let us: - validate profile behavior across hardware (A100/A10/GPU instances) and quantization modes - detect kernel-selection drift during compiler upgrades - provide a human-auditable trail (commit + benchmark snapshot) for release notes and customer-facing pin explainers
acceptance_criteria: A curated catalog entry exists for at least 3 model archetypes: (1) MHA-heavy baseline, (2) GQA variant with grouped attention, (3) MoE model with 16 experts; each entry contains compile flags, kernel versions, and provenance hash
Synthetic benchmark repo runs end-to-end in CI and produces stable latency distributions (P50/P95/P99) that match the documented reference within ±10% on target hardware
Pin-validation pipeline rejects profiles that increase P95 latency by >15% or change top-1 token distribution (surrogate quality) beyond tolerated threshold on smoke prompts
Publish process creates a signed profile artifact and a Confluence page with benchmark snapshots and migration notes
tasks: Design synthetic workload shapes (token length distributions, prefix reuse, expert routing ratios) — owner: Daniel
Implement benchmark harness (Docker + small python runner) with deterministic RNG seeds — owner: Priya
Add compile-provenance metadata to compiler artifacts (git sha, build flags, kernel version) — owner: Build Team
Create pin-validation CI job and gating webhook for profile registry — owner: Infra
Run multi-hardware sweep (A100, A10, T4) and collect artifacts — owner: SRE
Author Confluence playbook and internal release notes template — owner: Marisol
Add telemetry metrics and dashboard for profiling results and regression alerts — owner: Observability
rollout_plan: 1) Land benchmark harness and compile-metadata in a feature branch; 2) Run baseline sweep on staging machines, produce catalog draft; 3) Iterate with research for kernel hints where regressions appear; 4) Enable pin-validation as optional gate for one model-team (canary); 5) If canary stable for 2 weeks, flip to required for all profile publishes. Immediate fallback: profile registry supports automated rollback to most recent signed profile artifact.
test_plan: Unit tests for harness runner and deterministic seeds
CI integration that runs synthetic benchmark suite on PRs touching compiler/profile code
Golden snapshot comparisons stored as artifacts (latency histograms + kernel tables)
Small end-to-end smoke with real short prompts validating token output distributions
Chaos test: introduce a compiler change in sandbox and ensure pin-validation rejects if thresholds exceeded
risks_mitigations: Risk: Synthetic workloads may not cover edge-cases seen in the wild — Mitigation: pair with two customer workspaces to collect representative traces and add to benchmark shapes
Risk: Benchmark noise across hardware creates false positives — Mitigation: require multiple-run averaging, use controlled instance pools and seed affinities
Risk: Publishing friction slows onboarding velocity — Mitigation: provide opt-out for early teams and a fast-path with manual review
Risk: Large storage overhead for artifacts — Mitigation: compress artifacts, keep rolling 90-day retention, push key hashes to registry instead of full binary where possible
